edges.description: Chronic T-cell inflammation contributes to epithelial injury and oxidative stress.
edges.target: Basal Keratinocyte Injury and Oxidative Stress

edges.description: Chronic inflammation promotes tissue remodeling and sclerosis through incompletely resolved intermediates.
ECM1 autoantibodies have been proposed to alter MMP9 and TGF-beta activity, but causality and intermediate steps are not established.
Persistent epithelial injury and inflammation contribute to the fibrosing tissue-remodeling response.
edges.source: Basal Keratinocyte Injury and Oxidative Stress
Circumcision for Penile Scarring or Phimosis

nodes.description: Basal keratinocyte degeneration and oxidative damage accompany genital lichen sclerosus. Lipid peroxidation, oxidative DNA damage, and reduced antioxidant defenses are reported, but their position in the causal sequence remains provisional.
nodes.id: Basal Keratinocyte Injury and Oxidative Stress

evidence.snippet: Lipid peroxidation in keratinocytes, oxidative DNA damage and protein oxidation in areas of LS were associated with low concentrations of antioxidant enzymes

nodes.description: Complete circumcision is used for progressive fibrous phimosis and foreskin scarring in penile lichen sclerosus; persistent active disease may still require topical corticosteroid treatment and follow-up.
nodes.id: Circumcision for Penile Scarring or Phimosis

evidence.snippet: a frenuloplasty in the context of complete circumcision should be recommended

nodes.description: Fibroblast proliferation and increased collagen I and III synthesis remodel the upper dermis, while basal keratinocyte degeneration and epidermal atrophy weaken the epithelial surface. These changes produce the hallmark white atrophic lesions, scarring, and site-specific functional sequelae.

biological_processes: Transforming growth factor beta receptor signaling pathway

evidence.snippet: Another characteristic of LS is the augmented collagen synthesis in the dermis, in particular, collagen I and III.

nodes.description: Pain during intercourse due to introital narrowing, fissuring, and inelastic scarred tissue.

evidence.snippet: narrowing of vaginal introitus can occasionally lead to dyspareunia

nodes.description: Circulating IgG autoantibodies recognize extracellular matrix protein 1 (ECM1) in many patients. The immune response is reproducible, but whether it drives matrix injury or is partly an epiphenomenon remains uncertain.

evidence.reference_title: Autoantibodies to extracellular matrix protein 1 in lichen sclerosus.
evidence.snippet: These findings provide evidence for a specific humoral immune response to ECM1 in lichen sclerosus
The significance of the autoantibodies is unclear and, except for anti-EMC1 antibodies, they may only represent an epiphenomenon rather than a key-component of the LS pathogenesis

nodes.description: Fibrotic scarring can resorb or fuse vulvar structures, narrow the introitus, or create foreskin and glans adhesions.

evidence.snippet: Scarring often results in fusion or even complete resorption of labia minora and loss of clitoral hood.

nodes.description: Ivory-white, waxy, atrophic macules, papules, or plaques on affected genital skin.

evidence.snippet: The typical clinical picture includes chronic whitish atrophic patches along with itching and soreness in the vulvar, perianal and penile regions.

nodes.description: Progressive preputial scarring can prevent foreskin retraction.

evidence.reference_title: Balanitis Xerotica Obliterans (Male Penile Lichen Sclerosus).
evidence.snippet: Involvement of the foreskin leads to atrophic skin changes with depigmentation and constriction, which can result in phimosis.

nodes.description: Itching of affected genital skin, often accompanied by soreness or burning.

evidence.snippet: The clinical picture of anogenital LS (gLS) includes ivory-white patches, atrophy and severe pruritus

nodes.description: Genital lichen sclerosus lesions contain dermal T-cell infiltrates with CD8 and regulatory T cells and a smaller CD4 component. CXCR3/CCR5 expression and interferon-gamma production support a Th1-skewed inflammatory profile, but the initiating antigen and exact causal sequence remain unresolved.

evidence.snippet: The involved cells express the chemokine receptors CXCR3 and CCR5 and lack CCR3 and CCR4, suggesting a Th1 profile.

nodes.description: An ultrapotent topical corticosteroid used to induce control of active genital lichen sclerosus and continued or intermittent maintenance according to clinical response.

evidence.reference_title: Treatment of male genital lichen sclerosus with clobetasol propionate and maintenance with either methylprednisolone aceponate or tacrolimus: a retrospective study.
evidence.snippet: Clobetasol propionate 0.05% cream is effective as first-line treatment in male GLS.
Topical glucocorticosteroids are the first-line therapy in gLS

nodes.description: Scar-mediated narrowing of the urethra is a recognized sequela of penile disease.

evidence.reference_title: Balanitis Xerotica Obliterans (Male Penile Lichen Sclerosus).
evidence.snippet: Urethral stricture disease, phimosis, and meatal stenosis are common sequelae of balanitis xerotica obliterans.
